newsitem.title: UK: Emerging market intl bonds total $10 bln in Jan 97.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market intl bonds total $10 bln in Jan 97.

text.p: Emerging market borrowers raised nearly $10 billion in the international bond markets in January, a near 60 percent rise over January 1996, Capital DATA Bondware figures showed.
Their total market share rose to 11 percent from eight percent last year.
Latin American borrowers issued over $5.5 billion, with Argentina contributing a hefty $2.5 billion. Mexico borrowed $1.3 billion and Brazilian names raised just under $1.0 billion.
Asia was the second-most active region with $2.8 billion of new deals. The Middle East raised $307 million and Eastern Europe $70 million.
Most of the money was borrowed in the dollar sector, which totalled $7.5 billion ($3.2 billion in 1996).
The Mexican and Argentine governments successfully issued jumbo, long-dated dollar global bonds in January, tapping into a wider investor base for high-yielding paper.
This so called cross-over buying -- when non-emerging market specialists buy emerging market debt -- has fuelled demand for dollar bonds and buoyed Latin American bond spreads.
During the whole of 1996, emerging market borrowers raised around $80 billion in the international bond markets.
Figures include Eurobonds, global bonds, Yankee bonds and Samurai bonds.
